full_judgment:
LATIFUR RAHMAN, J.: This appeal by leave by the Auction Purchaser-appellant is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.6.90 of the. High Court Division; Dhaka passed in Civil Revision No. 438 of 1990 discharging the Rule, after affirming the order dated 27.1.90 passed in Money Execution Case No. 78 off 1984 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong. 

2. Respondent No. 3 as plaintiff institute Money Suit No. 161 of 1969 .in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and three others as defendants for recovery of Tk. 4,73,001. 35 with subsequent costs and interests alleging, inter alia, that the defendants in 1961 opened letter of credit with the plaintiff bank for importing machineries for setting up a Glass Factory at Nasirabad, Chittagong; that the Machineries were imported but the defendants neither established the factory nor paid back the amount to the plaintiff and hence the suit. 

3. Respondent No. 1, Company filed written statement duly verified by its Managing Director, respondent No. 2, but ulitmately did not contest the suit. The said suit on transfer to the Court of 3rd Subordinate Judge, Chittagong was renumbered as Money suit No. 36 of 1971 and was decreed ex-parte on 27.7.72. The said decree was put into execution in Money Execution Case No. 34 of 1982 of the 3rd Court of subordinate Judge, Chittagong. But after the abolition of the said Court the case was renumbered as Money Execution Case No. 78 of (11.1984 of the 2nd Court of subordinate Judge, Chittagong. Some of the imported machineries as described in schedule 1 of the plaint were stored and kept in the godown under the care and control of respondent No. 3-bank and in such circumstances respondent No. 3 filed an application on 18.11.82 under Order 21 Rule 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the executing Court of attachment and sale of the said machineries and the executing court allowed the said application by its order dated 3.2.83. Thereafter a notice was published in the daily Azadi on 19.9.88 of public auction of the said movables of the judgment-debtors on 5.11.88., Public auction of the said movables was accordingly held on 5.11.88 and the highest bid of the appellant for Tk. 2,52,500.00 was accepted and the appellant deposited the entire sale price of Tk. 2,52,500.00 in court by challan as per order of the Court. 

4. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application in the aforesaid Money Execution Case No. 78 of 1984 not to deliver the auction sold movables to the appellant till their filing a case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 27.7.72. Thereafter respondent Nos. 1 and 2 file another application on 11.12.88 under Section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code for cancellation of the auction sale and for return of the machineries to them on payment of Tk. 5 (live) lacs. The executing court disposed of the said two applications observing that the said application could be considered if the judgment-debtors deposit in court the entire decrial dues with interest and costs amounting to Tk. 6,19,578/29 within 22.12.88. On the application of the respondents time was subsequently extended upto 11.1.89 for depositing the decrial dues. 

5. On 31.12.88 respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 130 of 1988 for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 27.7.72. Respondents also filed an application in the said Miscellaneous case for stay of further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 78 of 1984 and 2.1.89 was fixed for hearing and disposal. A similar application for stay was also filed in the Money Execution Case no. 78 of 1984 on 1.1.89 which was rejected by the executing court by its order No. 83 dated 28.1.89. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 again on 9.2.89 filed another application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the executing court for staying further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the aforesaid Misc. Case No. 130 of 1988, but the learned Judge rejected the application by his Order No. 86 dated 13.2.89 and the execution case was ordered to be proceed with. Respondents thereafter filed successive petitions for time allowing them to bring stay order from the High Court Division and they having failed to bring the stay order, the executing court ordered to deliver the auction sold goods to the appellants whose bid was earlier accepted and who pad and deposited the price by challan on 15.11.88 as per order of the Court; but the auction sold goods were not delivered to the appellant 

6. Respondents Nos. 1 and 2 thereafter filed another application on 17.5.89 for time to bring stay order but the same was rejected. The said respondents then filed another application under Section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code for time for seven days to bring stay order but the same was also rejected on 18.5.89 and directions were issued to deliver the auction sold goods to the appellant but the same were not delivered. 

7. On 21.5.89 respondent Nos. 1 and 2 moved a revisiOnal application before the High Court Division, Chittagong but ulitimately withdrew the same as not pressed. The said respondents also filed two applications before the executing court on 21.5.89 one for seven days-time to bring stay order and the other for 15 days-time to deposit the decrial dues but both the applications were rejected. 
8. In the meantime the appellant sold the aforesaid auction purchased goods to one Parimal Bikash Sen at a total consideration of Tk.4.75 lacs by an agreement of sale with a stipulation that if the goods were not delivered to him he would get compensation of Tk. 1.00 lac which was also brought to the notice of the executing Court. 

9. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, however, on 22.6.89 ultimately deposited the decretal dues much out of time and the executing court by Order No. 127 dated 27.1.90 was pleased to pass order for release of the auction sold goods in favour of the Judgment -debtor-respondents and allowed the auction-purchaser appellant only compensation @ 10%. This order was challenged before the High Court Division in revision, being Civil Revision No. 438 of 1990 and the Rule was discharged. 

10. the learned Judges of the High Court-Division though found that the sale of goods in question became absolute under Order 21, Rule 77 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court has still the jurisdiction to set aside the sale under Section 151 of the code of civil procedure. The learned Judges after referring to a number of decisions, particularly the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109, held that the executing court rightly exercised its inherent power after considering the hardship of all concerned. 

11. leave was granted to consider whether the sale having become absolute under Order 21, Rule 77(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned Judges misdirected themselves in releasing the auction sold goods in favour of the judgment-debtor-respondents; whether to correct and true interpretation of Order 21, Rule 78 of the Code, could the learned Judges release the goods in favour of the judgment-debtor when, the sale is not a nullity and whether in vice of specific provisions of Rules 77 and 78 of Order  21 of the Code for Public auction of moveable property and remedy provided thereunder, section 151 of the Code is available in the instant case to set aside the sale. Leave was also granted to consider whether the High Court Division was wrong in assessing the compensation @ 10% in the face of the provision of Order 21, Rule 78 of the Code when the auction purchaser entered into an agreement for sale of the auction purchased moveable property with a 3rd party providing for compensation at Tk. 1 (one) lac. 
12. From the materials on record it appears that in the instant case the auction sale was held on 5.11.88 and on that day the Nazir of the Court submitted the proceeding before the executing court noting the amounts quoted by different tenderers and the executing court accepted the quotation of the auction purchaser-appellant being the highest bidder by an endorsement made in the body of the auction sheet by an order in the order sheet on 10.11.88 it was formally accepted and the auction purchaser was allowed time till 15.11.88 to deposit the entire bid money which was accordingly deposited on 15.11.88. 

Order 21, Rule 77, Sub-Rules 1 and 2 read as follows-

"77.-(1) Where moveable property is sold by public auction the price of each lot shall be paid at the time of sale or as soon after as the officer or Other person holding the sale directs and in default of payment the property shall forthwith be re-sold. 

(2), On payment of the purchase-money, the officer of other person holding the sale shall grant a receipt the same, and the sale shall become absolute." 

Thus, it appears that the appellant deposited the amount another the auction sale on 15.11.88 as per the order of the Court and after accepting the appellant. The auction sale of the tenant was formally accepted by the Court by order dated 10.11.88 giving time to the auction appellant to deposit the entire bid by 15.11.88 and the same was duly. As per Sub-Rule 2 of Rule 77 of the Code on payment of the purchase more by the sale became absolute and the same cannot be set aside in the manner as has been done by the executing court and affirmed by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. Further, a reference to Order 21, Rule 78 of the Code shows that for any irregularity in publishing or conducting the sale of moveable property the sale shall not be vitiated but a person sustaining any injury by such irregularity at the hand of any other person may institute a suit for compensation or for recovery of specific property and for compensation in default of such recovery. In the present case there being no allegation that the sale was a nullity, the same cannot be set aside as Rule 78 of Order 21 of the Code clearly speaks that for mere irregularity no sale shall be vitiated. Hence the learned Judges of the High Court Division without appreciating the true and correct import of Rules 77 an 78 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure set aside the auction sale. The case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109, is a case relating to auction sale of immoveable property wherein this Division after considering the case of both the parties in order to save the immoveable property of the appellant, an amount of Tk. 75,000/00 was directed to be paid to respondent No. 2 (highest bidder) as compensation as he was an innocent sufferer for the latches of the appellant. Thus, the case reported in 41 D.L.R. which relates to a immoveable property has no application in a sale of moveable property. Sale of immovable property is guided under Order 21, Rule 82 to 103 of the Code. Particularly Sale of immoveable property will become absolute and certificate will be issued under Rule 94 of Order 21 of the Code. The Court exercised its discretion when the sale had not become absolute but in the present case the executing court has exercised a discretion after the sale become absolute and the learned Judges of the High Court Division on a wrong reliance on the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109 upheld the exercise of that discretion. 

13. It may be mentioned here that specific provisions having been provided and ;r the Code of Civil Procedure for sale of moveable property by auction sale as contemplated in Order 21, Rules 77, 78 and 79, the learned Judges of the High Court division misdirected themselves in taking recourse to Section 151 of the Code of. Civil Procedure for setting aside the auction sale. The learned Judges also wrongly assessed compensation @ 10% when from the materials on record it appears that the auction purchaser-appellant entered into a contract with on Primal Bikash Sen to sell the moveable properties where in it was provided that upon the auction-purchaser's failure to deliver the auction purchased goods, the appellant would pay a compensation of Tk. 1 (one) lac to Parimal Bikash sen. It appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division illegally affirmed the order of the Subordinate Judge wherein he set aside the sale by exercising the inherent power of the Court under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thus the learned Judges did not act legally in affirming the order of the executing court. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. Consequently, the appeal is allowed with costs.

End.
